name: Lemlist
tagline: Send a modest compliant sequence from an authenticated domain and stop on replies

pricing.notes: Official Email Pro monthly seat price.

tiers.name: Email
tiers.limits: Unlimited users and email senders, 50,000 emails/month, Email & Phone Number Finder, 650M+ lead DB, unlimited contacts, warm-up/deliverability.

tiers.name: Multichannel
tiers.limits: Unlimited emails and messages/month, 5 senders/user, LinkedIn/SMS, WhatsApp add-on, dialer/VoIP, tasks.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Teams of 5+ users, custom users, unlimited email and messages, at least 5 senders/user, SSO/SAML, 1:1 onboarding.

pricing.hiddenCosts: Credits cost $10 per 1,000; verified emails cost 5 credits/email, phone numbers 20 credits/number, intent signals from 20 to 400+ credits.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Lemlist, send a modest compliant sequence from an authenticated domain and stop on replies. The hard boundary is deliverability tooling, warm-up network, personalization, data, and multichannel workflow, plus proprietary data, deliverability, and network effects.
coreLoopDIY: Import a permissioned lead list, personalize a modest compliant sequence sent from an authenticated domain, enforce sending limits, stop on replies, and track results without supplying proprietary contact data.
whatYouLose: deliverability tooling, warm-up network, personalization, data, and multichannel workflow
moatNotes: proprietary data, deliverability, and network effects
ongoingBurden: consent records, suppression lists, DNS, bounces, reputation, abuse complaints, provider limits, and changing email rules
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Lemlist because the durable value is accurate contact data and deliverability infrastructure; a sequence editor alone is not the product. The recurring cost buys consent records, suppression lists, DNS, bounces, reputation, abuse complaints, provider limits, and changing email rules, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Mautic
priorArt.desc: Open-source marketing automation platform with campaigns, contacts, and email workflows.

alternatives.name: Mautic
alternatives.desc: A campaign engine with reply, bounce and unsubscribe handling; personalized images and outreach theatre are gone.

rejectedAlternatives.name: listmonk
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A fine newsletter sender, but it does not watch replies and stop a sales sequence; wrong kind of email automation.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Email Pro plan and a small permission-based outreach console DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Lemlist in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and a user-chosen transactional email provider; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: import a permissioned lead list, personalize a modest compliant sequence sent from an authenticated domain, enforce sending limits, stop on replies, and track results without supplying proprietary contact data.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Accept CSV imports only after the user confirms lawful collection and records the source.
Provide contact fields, tags, suppression status, consent notes, and a complete change history.
Build a short email sequence with delays, business-hour windows, and per-domain rate limits.
Use the configured provider for sends and process delivery, bounce, complaint, and unsubscribe webhooks.
Stop sequences immediately on reply, bounce, complaint, suppression, or manual pause.
Show deliverability warnings, daily send totals, and a mandatory preview before activation.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out scraping protected platforms.
Deliberately leave out buying or generating personal contact data.
Deliberately leave out automated inbox warm-up networks and evasion of provider limits.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
